name: TeamStarWolf - Web Application Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of ATT&CK techniques commonly encountered during web application, API, and application-security testing. This is not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: WEB_APPLICATION_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, WEB_APPLICATION_PENTESTING.md, API_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, SECURE_CODING_REFERENCE.md, PENETRATION_TESTING_METHODOLOGY.md, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl.

techniques.comment: Core web/API exploitation technique cited by the web pentesting, API security, and secure coding references for injection, SSRF, and public-facing application compromise.
JavaScript execution covers XSS and client-side script abuse called out in the web application pentesting reference.
Command and scripting interpreter abuse covers command injection, template injection, unsafe deserialization, and other interpreter-driven web application attack paths.
Web shell deployment is explicitly mapped in the penetration testing methodology and is a common post-exploitation outcome for compromised web servers.
Server software component persistence generalizes web shell and server-extension abuse after application compromise.
Valid Accounts is cited for API credential stuffing, stolen JWT reuse, broken auth, and access-control abuse in the API and secure coding references.
Default accounts are included for default credential testing and exposed admin panels described in the web security and pentesting references.
Brute Force covers authentication abuse, account lockout failures, and credential-stuffing exposure discussed across the web, API, and secure coding references.
Password spraying is included for web and API login testing workflows in the penetration testing methodology.
Stealing web session cookies maps to session-management weaknesses, XSS impact, and missing HttpOnly/SameSite controls in the secure coding reference.
Unsecured Credentials covers API keys, secrets, cloud metadata credentials, and exposed configuration files highlighted in the API and secure coding references.
Credentials in files are included for .env, config, backup, and repository secret exposure paths described in the web security references.
Private keys are included for hardcoded credential and exposed-key findings in source, configuration, and deployment artifacts.
Proxy is included for SSRF-to-internal-service and proxy-abuse scenarios described in the web and secure coding references.
Multi-hop proxy represents chained proxying and SSRF pivoting patterns used to reach internal services through a vulnerable application.
Active scanning maps to web asset discovery, nuclei/nikto/testssl, and application reconnaissance workflows in the pentesting references.
Scanning IP blocks supports external exposure discovery and perimeter enumeration during web application assessments.
Vulnerability scanning covers nuclei, ZAP, Nikto, TLS scanners, and automated web/API assessment workflows referenced in the library.
Wordlist scanning maps to ffuf, gobuster, feroxbuster, parameter discovery, and forced browsing activities from the web pentesting reference.
DNS reconnaissance supports subdomain enumeration and certificate-transparency workflows used to build web application attack surface maps.
Network Service Discovery is cited in the API security reference for endpoint enumeration and in pentesting workflows for exposed service mapping.
Data from Cloud Storage maps to misconfigured APIs, presigned URLs, and cloud object storage exposure called out in the API security reference.
Exfiltration Over Web Service covers large API exports, HTTP exfiltration, and web-service data theft noted in the API and pentesting references.
Exfiltration to Cloud Storage is included for API and storage abuse paths involving cloud buckets, presigned URLs, and object storage.
Endpoint Denial of Service covers rate-limit failures, expensive API queries, large payloads, and resource exhaustion in the secure coding and API references.
Application or system exploitation captures application-layer DoS through expensive requests, parser abuse, and business-flow abuse.
Supply Chain Compromise is included for vulnerable/outdated components, CI/CD integrity failures, and dependency risk in the secure coding reference.
Compromised software dependencies and development tools covers dependency confusion, malicious packages, and build-chain exposure affecting web applications.
Exploitation for Client Execution covers vulnerable client-side components and browser exploitation paths surfaced by web application content.
Gather Victim Host Information is included for verbose errors, exposed technology fingerprints, and stack/version disclosure during web recon.
Software fingerprinting maps to Wappalyzer, WhatWeb, headers, cookies, error pages, and JavaScript-library discovery in the web references.
Indicator Removal is included for logging and monitoring failures, log tampering concerns, and missing audit trails in web and API environments.
